rows.description: A child insists his favourite cricketer is the best and only remembers the matches that prove it. Bad scores are explained away as bad luck or a bad umpire.

rows.description: A teenager who has decided a classmate is fake reads every message for proof and skips anything friendly. Feeds and group chats keep serving what already fits.

rows.description: A college student picks articles and seniors' advice that back a decision already made, such as skipping placements, and feels well researched while only collecting agreement.

rows.description: A roommate sees a friend dismiss every warning about a shaky startup idea while quoting each encouraging comment. Naming the pattern kindly works better than arguing point by point.

rows.description: A young professional decides early that a new colleague is weak and then reads each small slip as confirmation while ignoring her good work. The first impression quietly steers later evidence.

rows.description: A mature worker asks what evidence would change her mind, seeks a smart critic, and reads the best case against her position before committing. Disagreement becomes data instead of insult.

rows.description: A child bargaining for stickers hears the first price and treats it as the fair baseline. Any lower number feels like a big win even when it is still too high.

rows.description: A graduate hears the first offer or the first quoted rent and adjusts too little from it. Even an arbitrary opening figure pulls the final agreement toward itself.
